candidates.label: Tarsus (modern city center)
candidates.support: The modern city of Tarsus overlies the ancient site, historically known also as Antiochia ad Cydnum; continuous occupation and identification are undisputed.

summary.text: Tarsus was, per Pleiades, 'an important city and river port on the Cydnus river located in Cilicia Pedias,' and, according to Acts, the birthplace of Paul, who identifies himself as 'a citizen of no insignificant city.'

history.text: Between about AD 37 and 41, Caligula gave parts of Cilicia to the client king Antiochus IV of Commagene and folded the rest, including the plain around Tarsus (Cilicia Pedias), into the province of Syria; a separate, reunified province of Cilicia was not re-established until Vespasian did so in AD 72. On this evidence, Tarsus's territory was administered as part of Syria at AD 50, matching the New Testament's own pairing of 'the regions of Syria and Cilicia' (Galatians 1:21; Acts 15:23, 41).

scripture.textWEB: The Lord said to him, “Arise and go to the street which is called Straight, and inquire in the house of Judah for one named Saul, a man of Tarsus. For behold, he is praying,
When the brothers knew it, they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
Barnabas went out to Tarsus to look for Saul.
But Paul said, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.”

“I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict tradition of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as you all are today.
